classification.difficultyReason: Construct a rational-assumption contradiction and generalise it using unique prime factorisation; part b must also exclude integers containing only 2 and 5 with unequal exponents.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $\log_{10}3$ cannot be a rational number.

answer.short:
$\log_{10}3$ is irrational.

A rational value would give $10^p=3^q$ for positive integers $p,q$, contradicting unique prime factorisation.
answer.worked:
Suppose $\log_{10}3=\frac{p}{q}$ for positive integers $p,q$.

$$\begin{align*}10^{p/q}&=3\\10^p&=3^q\\2^p5^p&=3^q\end{align*}$$

The left side has prime factors 2 and 5, whereas the right side has only prime factor 3. This contradicts unique prime factorisation. Therefore $\log_{10}3$ is irrational.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that $\log_{10}n$ cannot be a rational number if $n$ is any positive integer that is not a whole number power of 10.

answer.short:
$\log_{10}n$ is irrational whenever the positive integer $n$ is not a whole number power of 10.

If it were rational, unique prime factorisation would force $n=10^k$ for a nonnegative integer $k$.
answer.worked:
Since $n$ is not a whole number power of 10, $n\ne1$, so $n>1$. Suppose $\log_{10}n=\frac{p}{q}$ for positive integers $p,q$.

$$\begin{align*}10^{p/q}&=n\\10^p&=n^q\\2^p5^p&=n^q\end{align*}$$

By unique prime factorisation, $n$ has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Write $n=2^r5^s$, where $r,s$ are nonnegative integers. Then

$$\begin{align*}2^p5^p&=2^{rq}5^{sq}\\p&=rq\\p&=sq\\r&=s\end{align*}$$

Thus $n=2^r5^r=10^r$, contradicting the given condition. Therefore $\log_{10}n$ is irrational.
